transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, I'm here because for months now, I’ve just been seeing this exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, bills show up wrong, and people just conveniently forget to call me back. 

And, you know, even when everyone tells me it’s just administrative mistakes or whatever, I know better. I know they’re deliberately keeping information from me. It's pretty clear they're trying to push me out of making decisions.
Do you think someone is intentionally trying to harm you or your interests?

Yes, I do. Like I was just saying, it all comes back to that same pattern. The moved appointments for my sister, the messed up bills, people conveniently forgetting to call me back... it's too consistent to just be a coincidence. 

Even though everyone else tries to brush it off as simple mistakes, I know they are doing it on purpose. They are intentionally keeping information away from me because they want to push me out of making decisions. So, yes, they are absolutely trying to undermine my interests.
Do you believe there is a specific group or person behind these attempts to undermine your interests?

Well, I'm not exactly sure who it is, specifically. I mean, I don't have names or anything like that. It just feels like... like a coordinated effort by the people handling her care and the administration. But no, I can't point to one specific person or a named group. It's just the people involved in all this paperwork and scheduling.
Do you think these people are trying to harm you directly or just undermine your interests?

I don't think they're trying to physically hurt me, if that's what you mean. It's not like I'm worried for my safety. It's more about my sister's care and my role in it. They're just trying to cut me out, to undermine my authority and my ability to make sure she's getting what she needs. That's the part they're targeting.
Have you ever had a period of time where you didn't think someone was trying to undermine your interests?

Yes, definitely. I mean, before all this started, everything was fine. This whole situation has only been going on for about 11 months now. It started right around the time my sister's health suddenly got worse, and I had to step in and start coordinating all her care. Before that, I didn't have any reason to think anyone was working against me.
Do you still believe that people are intentionally trying to undermine your interests when you're not actively thinking about your sister's care?

Well, it's really just tied to her situation. Outside of dealing with my sister's appointments and trying to get straight answers from those people, I don't feel like that. I just go about my normal day. 

I still keep my home in order, I pay my bills, I go in and do my job. I know some people might think I'm a little too focused on this whole thing with her care, but... I'm not falling apart or acting strangely in other parts of my life. The interference is strictly happening with the people handling her case. When I'm away from that, everything else is just normal.
Do you ever have times when you don't think someone is trying to undermine your interests related to your sister's care, even when you are directly dealing with it?

No, not really. Whenever I'm dealing with it, the pattern is just... it's always there. For months now, I've been seeing the exact same things happen. Her appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the medical bills show up with all these errors, and the staff constantly "forget" to call me back. 

I know they all say these are just clerical mistakes or scheduling issues, but... I know better. It's too consistent. They are deliberately keeping information from me. They're doing it on purpose to push me out of the decision-making process for her. So, no, when I'm dealing with her care, I never think it's just an accident.
Are there any other areas of your life where you feel like someone is intentionally trying to undermine you or keep information from you?

No, not at all. Like I said, it's really just isolated to my sister's situation. At work, my team and I get along fine. Nobody is messing with my files or trying to go behind my back there. And with my friends or neighbors, everything is completely normal. I don't have any issues with anyone else. It's strictly the people involved in my sister's medical care. That's the only place where this is happening.
Have you ever considered the possibility that the issues with your sister's care might be due to genuine mistakes rather than intentional actions?

No, I haven't. I mean, I know that's what everyone else says. They say, "Oh, it's just a scheduling error," or "It's a clerical mistake." But... I'm here because for months now, I've been seeing the exact same pattern. 

It's not just one or two things. It's her appointments getting moved constantly, the bills showing up wrong over and over, the staff always "forgetting" to call me back. Even when everyone tries to tell me it's just mistakes, I know better. I know they're deliberately keeping information from me. They are trying to push me out of the decisions about her care. It's too consistent to be an accident.
Have you ever considered that you might be wrong about people intentionally trying to undermine your interests?

Honestly, no. I know I'm repeating myself here, but... I don't think I'm wrong. I'm here because I have been seeing this exact same pattern for months now. My sister's appointments get moved around, the bills show up wrong, people constantly 'forget' to call me back. 

Even when everyone around me says it's just mistakes or coincidences, I know what I'm looking at. I know they're keeping information from me on purpose. They are trying to push me out of the decisions regarding her care. So, no, I don't believe I'm wrong about what they're doing.
Has your belief that people are intentionally trying to undermine your interests in your sister's care ever changed or wavered since it started?

No, it hasn't wavered at all. I know I keep saying the same thing, but it's the truth. For months now, I've been dealing with this exact same pattern. Her appointments get shifted around without warning, the billing is constantly messed up, and the staff always seem to "forget" to return my calls. People keep trying to tell me it's just a series of mistakes, but I know what's really going on. They are deliberately keeping information from me and actively trying to push me out of making decisions for her. I haven't doubted that for a second.
Have you considered taking legal action against those you believe are undermining your interests in your sister's care?

I haven't really thought about a lawsuit or anything like that. I mean, I don't even know who I would sue, exactly. It's not just one person, it's... the whole system they have set up. I just want it to stop. I want them to stop messing with her care and trying to cut me out of it. Going to a lawyer just seems like it would take years and... well, I don't have that kind of time when it comes to my sister's well-being. I just need them to do their jobs and include me like they're supposed to.
Have you ever had any doubts about your belief that people are intentionally trying to undermine your interests in your sister's care?

No, I haven't. I know we just talked about this, but I really haven't had any doubts. I've been seeing this same pattern for months. It's the moved appointments, the incorrect bills, the unreturned phone calls. 

People keep telling me it's just human error or coincidences, but I know better. They are deliberately keeping information from me. They want to push me out of the decisions regarding her care, and I am absolutely certain of that.
Can you think of any specific incident where you felt someone was trying to undermine your interests that didn't involve your sister's care?

No, not really. It's... it's just about my sister. I don't have these kinds of problems at work or with my neighbors or anything like that. It's specifically the people involved in her care facility and her doctors. That's where all this is happening. Outside of that, things are pretty normal.
Have you experienced any significant life changes or stressful events outside of your sister's health issues in the past year?

No, not really. Aside from everything going on with my sister, my life is pretty stable. Work is fine, nothing major has changed there. I'm still doing the same job, supervising my team. No big moves, no financial crises or anything like that. It's really just the stress of dealing with her care facility and the people there. That's the only thing that's been overwhelming. Everything else is just... normal.
Have you ever considered seeking a second opinion on your sister's care from a different doctor or medical facility?

No, I haven't. I mean, why would I? It wouldn't really solve the problem. The issue isn't that I think her current doctors are incompetent medically, it's that they—along with the facility staff—are actively trying to shut me out. 

If I just moved her to another facility or got a second opinion, what's to stop the new people from doing the exact same thing? Or what if these current people just contact the new ones and poison the well? The medical care itself isn't the part I'm questioning, it's the... the deliberate obstruction. So, no, a second opinion wouldn't fix what's actually going on.
Can you describe the very first incident that made you think someone was intentionally trying to undermine your interests in your sister's care?

Well, it started about 11 months ago. That was when my sister's health suddenly took a turn for the worse, and I had to step in and really start coordinating her care. I remember going to the facility to check on a change in her medication, and the charge nurse just... wouldn't give me a straight answer. She kept talking around it, looking at me like I had no right to ask. That was the first time I realized they were deliberately keeping things from me. It's been going on ever since.
Have you ever felt like the people involved in your sister's care were not trying to undermine you during any specific interaction or meeting with them?

No, honestly, I haven't. I mean, I'm here because for months now I've been seeing the exact same pattern, over and over. My sister's appointments get moved without anyone telling me, the billing statements show up with all these errors, and people conveniently "forget" to call me back. 

Whenever I confront them about it, everyone just says it's administrative mistakes or short-staffing. But it's too consistent. I know they're deliberately keeping information from me and trying to push me out of making decisions for her. So no, there hasn't been a time where I felt they weren't doing this. It's constant.
